item.title: 0.3.3-beta.8
item.description:
Aki 0.3.3 beta 8

  • The tag over what you point at says "↑ bigger · ↓ smaller": ↑ takes what holds it — a block, the whole terminal, the window.
  • Each build's number now includes the second, so two versions built close together both reach you.

item.title: 0.3.3-beta.7
item.description:
Aki 0.3.3 beta 7

  • The sidebar's resize corner stays visible however often the pointer goes back and forth over it.

item.title: 0.3.3-beta.6
item.description:
Aki 0.3.3 beta 6

  • Orca's pop-ups and buttons can be marked (Orca answered with a see-through layer over its whole window).
  • The sidebar's rings show just the number of waiting marks, without a tiny crop beside it.

Aki 0.3.2

Updates, like they should be

  • A new version shows as a pill by the sidebar. Click it and it downloads right there — a bar filling up, Aki's pin riding its tip — then Aki restarts by itself on the new version and says so. No more update windows.
  • Aki looks for a new version every hour.

Marking

  • The comment card can be dragged by its top, off what you want to see.
  • The queue's destination is a clear field: the AI, the app and the session's whole name.

Privacy, said plainly

  • Aki sends anonymous notices to its maker when it's installed and when it updates: its version (and the one before), your macOS version and language. No account, no identifier, nothing you mark. They tell how many people use Aki and on which version, so the right things get fixed first. Get started says so, and one switch turns them off (also in Settings → General → Privacy).

Aki 0.3.1

Fix

  • Pointing inside apps that tell macOS nothing about their window (Telegram) now picks the message, button or icon under the pointer. In 0.3.0 it still took the whole window there.

Aki 0.3.0

Mark anything, even where apps say nothing

  • Apps that don't tell macOS what's in their window (Telegram, games, some design apps) and pages drawn as one picture (Google Sheets): Aki now finds the box under the pointer in the screen itself — a message, a row, a button, an icon, a photo, a single spreadsheet cell. ↑ takes what holds it.
  • ⇧-click is a normal click on the app below (another sheet, a tab, a menu), without making a mark. A point is now ⌘-click.
  • ⌘+ / ⌘− zoom the page below while you mark.
  • Zoom on any mark's picture, from the card, the queue or the History.

The queue

  • Shows every mark, can be moved out of the way, and marks can be ticked and removed together (⌫).
  • The History shows what's waiting in the queue: keep marking with it, drop one, or clear it.

Faster, and to the right session

  • Marking opens at once, with the session you last wrote in as the destination.
  • The session picker shows four sessions, the rest behind "+N", each with whether it's working or waiting for you.
  • Marks go to the terminal 3 s after you stop (was 5 s).
  • Updates are announced, not downloaded: a pill by the sidebar and a dot on the menu bar pin.

Fixes

  • Sessions take the name you gave their tab in Orca.
  • Marks reach Orca tabs again after Orca restarts.
  • The sidebar's resize corner works next to the last ring.
